briefing:
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The past 24 hours indicate a significant increase in regional tensions, with heightened rhetoric from both US and Israeli leadership suggesting potential renewed military action against Iran. Compounding this, Israel has sustained notable military casualties in southern Lebanon, including an officer killed by a Hezbollah drone, while simultaneously conducting extensive strikes against Hezbollah targets. Reports of secret Israeli military bases in Iraq and a drone attack on a UAE nuclear plant underscore the expanding geographical scope and complexity of the conflict.

IRAN
Military operations in and against Iran include Abu Dhabi's report of a drone attack on an electrical generator outside the Barakah Nuclear Power Plant in the Al Dhafra Region, causing a fire but no radiological safety impact. A fire was reported at an oil factory in Maragheh, northwestern Iran, and a 2,000-pound MK-84 bomb was safely neutralized underground in Delfan, western Iran, after six days of excavation. The spokesperson of Iran's Armed Forces, General Shekarchi, warned that any repeat of folly by the US against Iran would lead to "harsher and more powerful blows." Internally, Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf, the Parliament Speaker, was appointed as Iran’s special representative for China’s affairs. Some sources, including @mamlekate and @kianmeli1 (attributing to Abtahi), refer to the "killed leader of the Islamic Republic," implying the demise of Ali Khamenei, and discuss a potential succession ("if a second Khamenei was not elected, civil war was certain"), while other Iranian sources (Press TV, Shargh) continue to refer to "the Leader of the Islamic Revolution" and his advisor without explicitly confirming a death or succession, creating a significant contradiction in reporting on Iranian leadership. Economically, Iran's stock exchange is set to reopen on Tuesday, the first time since late February. Oil prices jumped to over $109 per barrel. Negotiations with the US are ongoing, with Washington reportedly demanding no reparations, transfer of 400kg of enriched uranium, one operational nuclear facility, release of less than 25% of frozen funds, and a ceasefire linked to negotiation. Iran's counter-conditions include an end to war on all fronts (especially Lebanon), lifting all sanctions, releasing all frozen funds, compensation for war damages, and recognition of Iran's sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz. Maritime traffic in the Strait of Hormuz has largely halted, with limited movement for Iran-linked vessels, prompting Iran to launch "Hormuz Safe," a maritime cargo insurance system with Bitcoin payments. Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister stated that enemy military equipment will no longer be allowed to pass through the Strait of Hormuz.

ISRAEL
Israeli military operations included the killing of two Palestinian terror operatives in Gaza who posed an immediate threat to forces. Specific individuals killed include Khamer Iyad Muhammad Al-Matouq and Khaled Muhammad Salem Jouda (Hamas operatives involved in the October 7 onslaught) in northern Gaza, and Abdel Rahman Mahmoud Jumaa Shafi (Hamas Bureij Battalion member) in central Gaza. IDF forces also neutralized Ez Ad-Din al-Hadad, described as Hamas's military wing commander and "number one in Hamas," along with his wife and daughter in Gaza. In southern Lebanon, the IDF struck approximately 100 Hezbollah targets over the weekend, including surveillance posts, weapon depots, and terror infrastructure, notably in the Tyre area. An Israeli Air Force strike also killed two Hezbollah operatives at a rocket-launching site following an attack on IDF troops. The Israeli Air Force successfully intercepted several rockets fired by Hezbollah into southern Lebanon. A suspicious aerial target detected over southern Lebanon was also intercepted, with no casualties reported. Casualties included the death of Cpt. Maoz Israel Recanati, 24, from Itamar, a platoon commander in the Golani Brigade's 12th Battalion, killed in a Hezbollah explosive drone attack in southern Lebanon, making him the seventh IDF soldier killed in southern Lebanon since the start of a ceasefire and the 20th since the Iran war escalated. Additionally, four soldiers were wounded in southern Lebanon by a roadside bomb, with one in serious condition and one moderately hurt. On the home front, a large explosion at the state-owned Tomer rocket propulsion facility near Beit Shemesh was reported, with authorities claiming it was a controlled test, though some sources disputed this, citing unusual scale and lack of prior warning. Political decisions saw the government approve the transfer of the National Digital Array to the Prime Minister's office and endorse the recognition of Jerusalem as Israel's capital, offering incentives for foreign embassies to relocate. Prime Minister Netanyahu stated he would discuss Iran with President Trump, reiterating Israel's preparedness for "every scenario." He also claimed the mission of eliminating all architects of the October 7 massacre was "very close to completion." Discussions are set to resume in the Foreign Affairs and Defense Committee on a draft exemption law for Haredim and the extension of mandatory military service, with reports of Haredi parties threatening to dissolve the Knesset if the exemption law is not passed. MK Moshe Arbel resigned from the Knesset for personal reasons. The Israeli economy contracted by 3.3% in Q1 2026 due to the Iran war. New York Times reports revealed that Israel secretly operated at least two military bases in western Iraq since late 2024, one of which was used during the June 2025 war against Iran, with US knowledge and Iraqi radar systems reportedly deactivated to protect American aircraft.

GAZA & WEST BANK
Ground operations in Gaza included IDF forces killing armed Palestinian terror operatives in the southern and central parts of the Strip who posed immediate threats. Specifically, Hamas operatives Khamer Iyad Muhammad Al-Matouq and Khaled Muhammad Salem Jouda, identified as participants in the October 7 onslaught, were killed in northern Gaza. Abdel Rahman Mahmoud Jumaa Shafi, a Hamas Bureij Battalion member, was also killed in central Gaza. The most significant casualty reported was Ez Ad-Din al-Hadad, a senior commander of Hamas's military wing, who was killed along with his wife and daughter. Humanitarian conditions saw Israeli settlers continuing to force Palestinians to abandon villages in the occupied northern West Bank, and reports indicated Israel is blocking International Red Cross access to Palestinian abductees in prisons, hindering monitoring of their conditions. A mass wedding was held in Gaza City for couples whose marriages were delayed by the war and displacement. A branch of Bank al-Quds in Jabalia, northern Gaza, was reportedly attacked by the Israeli Air Force. While one Israeli source (Yediot News 25) reported a US State Department announcement of a 45-day extension to the Israel-Lebanon ceasefire, Hezbollah condemned al-Hadad's assassination as a violation of a standing ceasefire, implying such an agreement exists. Settler activity continues to be a concern, with Israeli Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir reportedly revealing schemes for illegal settlement expansion into southern Lebanon and renewing calls for the expulsion of Palestinians from Gaza and the West Bank. Reports also indicate Israeli authorities are using military infrastructure to facilitate the expansion of illegal settlements in the West Bank.

LEBANON
Hezbollah operations intensified, with the group claiming 19 military operations against Israeli positions, troops, and equipment over the past 24 hours along the border and deeper into southern Lebanon. These included launching multiple rockets and explosive drones at Israeli troops, some of which were intercepted by air defenses. One explosive drone triggered sirens in Misgav Am. Hezbollah's actions resulted in significant Israeli casualties, including the killing of Cpt. Maoz Israel Recanati, a platoon commander, by an explosive drone, and four Israeli soldiers wounded by a roadside bomb, one severely. Hezbollah released footage of operations targeting a wireless communication system in Blat, a Humvee in Naqoura-Alexandroun, and an armored personnel carrier in Bint Jbeil, and claimed to have set a Merkava tank on fire in Al-Bayada. Israeli strikes in response were extensive, with the IDF reporting attacks on approximately 100 Hezbollah targets across southern Lebanon over the weekend, including surveillance posts, weapon depots, and terror infrastructure, notably in the Tyre area. The IDF also confirmed striking in Ma'arub and Sukhmor in the Beqaa Valley. No UNIFIL incidents were reported. The IDF issued warnings to residents of the villages of al-Mrouaniyeh, Arazi (Sidon), al-Babeliyeh, and Basriyahu to move at least 1,000 meters away from their villages due to military activity. Cross-border exchanges were frequent, with Israeli air defenses intercepting rockets and suspicious aerial targets originating from Lebanon in several northern Israeli communities including Metula, Manara, Margaliot, Shlomi, Hanita, Betzet, Metzuba, Lehman, and Rosh HaNikra.

SYRIA & IRAQ
In Syria, Israeli occupation forces conducted new ground incursions into Quneitra province, ransacking houses, and an incursion into Daraa province with three tanks and a Dushka machine gun, firing at passersby. Explosions were reported in Izra (Daraa) and the Damascus countryside. In Iraq, a senior commander of Iraq's Hezbollah Brigades, Mohammed Baqer al-Saadi, was arrested by the US in Turkey and extradited to face terrorism charges, accused of planning at least 18 attacks in Europe, the US, and Canada in response to US-Israeli actions against Iran. The Iraqi Parliament requested international action regarding al-Saadi's abduction. Influential Iraqi cleric Muqtada al-Sadr congratulated Prime Minister Ali Faleh al-Zaidi on forming the government, urging the preservation of national sovereignty, combating corruption, and improving services. The New York Times reported that Israel secretly operated at least two military bases in western Iraq since late 2024, one of which was used during the June 2025 war with Iran. Iraqi security officials informed the NYT that the US had instructed Iraq to deactivate its radar systems during confrontations with Iran to protect American aircraft, leading Iraq to suspect the presence of Israeli forces. US fuel aircraft activity was observed in Anbar province, western Iraq, reportedly originating from Ben Gurion airport, suggesting combat and reconnaissance flights in Iraqi airspace. A drone attack on Iranian Kurdish opposition sites was reported in Sulaymaniyah, northern Iraq.

GULF STATES
The United Arab Emirates (UAE) reported a drone attack on an electrical generator outside the inner perimeter of the Barakah Nuclear Power Plant in the Al Dhafra Region, causing a fire but no casualties or impact on radiological safety. The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) confirmed that the radiation levels at Barakah were within the normal range. The Trump administration is reportedly encouraging the UAE to become more deeply involved in the Iran war, including potentially seizing Iranian Gulf islands such as Lavan. Kuwait arrested Iranian IRGC personnel in its waters, with reports showing images of their surrender. Bahraini scholars called on Islamic authorities worldwide to condemn the Al Khalifah regime's intensified crackdown on the country's Shia community, with protests held nationwide. Tensions in the Strait of Hormuz remained high, with shipping traffic largely halted, moving only vessels linked to Iran. Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister stated that enemy military equipment will no longer be allowed to pass through the Strait of Hormuz. South Korea's Foreign Minister Cho Hyun demanded an explanation from his Iranian counterpart, Seyed Abbas Araqchi, regarding an attack on the South Korean cargo ship HMM Namu near the Strait, which Iran denied, though both ministers agreed to maintain close communication to ensure maritime safety. Economically, oil prices jumped to over $109 per barrel. Iran launched a new maritime cargo insurance system, "Hormuz Safe," for vessels transiting the Strait, with Bitcoin payments.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **Imminent Iran War Threat:** US President Trump posted "This was the calm before the storm" on social media, while a US official indicated Trump is close to greenlighting military action against Iran. Netanyahu also stated he would speak with Trump and Israel is "prepared for every scenario" regarding Iran.
2.  **Israeli Bases in Iraq Revealed:** The New York Times reported that Israel secretly operated at least two military bases in western Iraq since late 2024, with one used during the June 2025 war against Iran, with US awareness and Iraq's radar systems reportedly deactivated.
3.  **Hezbollah Kills IDF Officer in Lebanon:** Cpt. Maoz Israel Recanati, 24, a platoon commander in the Golani Brigade, was killed by a Hezbollah explosive drone in southern Lebanon, with four other soldiers wounded by a roadside bomb.
4.  **Drone Attack on UAE Nuclear Plant:** Abu Dhabi confirmed a drone attack on an electrical generator outside the Barakah Nuclear Power Plant, causing a fire, but with no reported casualties or radiological impact.
5.  **Hamas Commander Assassinated:** Ez Ad-Din al-Hadad, a senior commander of Hamas's military wing, was killed in Gaza along with his wife and daughter.
6.  **Iraqi Hezbollah Commander Arrested:** Mohammed Baqer al-Saadi, a senior commander of Iraq's Hezbollah Brigades, was arrested by the US on terrorism charges related to planning multiple attacks in Europe, the US, and Canada.
7.  **Strait of Hormuz Tensions:** Maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz is largely halted, with Iran launching a new Bitcoin-based insurance system for transiting vessels and warning against military equipment passage.
8.  **Internal Israeli Political Crisis:** Debates on a Haredi draft exemption law and extension of mandatory service are ongoing in the Knesset, with Haredi parties reportedly threatening to dissolve the government over the issue, and MK Moshe Arbel resigned.
9.  **Conflicting Reports on Iranian Supreme Leader:** Multiple sources refer to the "killed leader of the Islamic Republic" (Ali Khamenei), while others continue to refer to "the Leader of the Islamic Revolution" and his advisors, without explicit confirmation of a death or succession.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks are extremely high, particularly between the US, Israel, and Iran. President Trump's strong rhetoric ("calm before the storm," "fire!"), coupled with reports of US officials indicating an imminent green light for military action against Iran, suggest a significant probability of renewed US-Israeli military operations. Iran's Armed Forces spokesperson warned of "harsher and more powerful blows" in retaliation to any aggression, and Iran's stated intention to deny military equipment passage through the Strait of Hormuz raises the stakes. Active flashpoints include southern Lebanon, where Hezbollah-Israel exchanges have resulted in significant casualties on both sides and extensive Israeli strikes, and the Gaza Strip, where IDF operations continue to target Hamas leadership. The Strait of Hormuz remains a critical flashpoint due to shipping disruptions, Iran's new maritime insurance, and warnings against military passage. Military posture changes include reports of US "high-level air force movements" in the Middle East, though 12 C-17A Globemaster III transport aircraft are reportedly leaving the region for Europe. The USS Gerald R. Ford carrier strike group has returned to the US after an 11-month deployment. Red lines include Iran's warning against attacks on its oil facilities, threatening reciprocal strikes on regional oil infrastructure, and its stance on the Strait of Hormuz.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The **United States** posture is overtly aggressive, with President Trump posting strong warnings ("calm before the storm") and discussing Iran with Prime Minister Netanyahu. A US official indicated Trump is close to greenlighting military action, and the White House warned against harming Americans. The Trump administration is reportedly encouraging the UAE to consider seizing Iranian Gulf islands. The US allowed a sanctions waiver permitting the purchase of Russian oil cargoes to expire. **Gulf states** are directly impacted: the **UAE** reported a drone attack on its Barakah Nuclear Power Plant, and **Kuwait** arrested Iranian IRGC personnel. **Bahraini** scholars and protesters condemned the regime's crackdown on the Shia community. **South Korea** demanded an explanation from Iran regarding an attack on its cargo ship HMM Namu near the Strait of Hormuz, with both nations' Foreign Ministers agreeing to maintain communication on maritime safety. In **Europe**, EU foreign policy chief Kalas cautioned that bombing Iranian facilities would not resolve issues and called for de-escalation, while Italy's Prime Minister canceled a diplomatic visit due to an internal security incident. **Russia** criticized a US/Bahraini draft resolution on the Strait of Hormuz as "not right" and its representative to international organizations warned of a possible imminent US-Israeli attack on Iran. **China** confirmed the appointment of Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf as Iran's special representative for Chinese affairs and reiterated its role as a "partner of peace" in the Middle East. President Putin is scheduled to visit China on Tuesday. **Pakistan's** Interior Minister visited Tehran to revive US-Iran peace talks and agreed on border trade facilitation, while the Pakistani army issued a strong warning to India against threatening a nuclear neighbor. **Brazil's** President Lula da Silva expressed opposition to the war in Iran and US intervention in Venezuela, also condemning the "genocide in Palestine" and sharing the 2010 nuclear deal document with Trump. The **International Criminal Court (ICC)** officially denied issuing new arrest warrants against Israel, although reports clarified that the prosecutor had requested five new warrants, with a decision still pending.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Significant contradictions persist in reporting, most notably regarding the status of **Iran's Supreme Leader**. Multiple sources (@mamlekate, @kianmeli1) refer to "the killed leader of the Islamic Republic" and discuss a succession crisis, while Iranian state-controlled media (Press TV, SharghDaily) continue to refer to "the Leader of the Islamic Revolution" and his advisors without explicitly confirming a death or succession. This represents a critical and unconfirmed discrepancy in core information about Iranian leadership. Another contradiction concerns the **Beit Shemesh explosion** in Israel; Israeli military and news sources (@N12, IDF, Faytuks) reported it as a controlled test at the Tomer rocket propulsion facility, while other sources (NAYA, @kianmeli1) questioned this narrative, citing the scale of the blast and the lack of prior public warning. Furthermore, the **ICC arrest warrant situation** saw conflicting initial reports of a denial, later clarified that the prosecutor had requested new warrants, but no decision was yet made. A claim by @yediotnews25 about a **45-day ceasefire extension between Israel and Lebanon**, attributed to the US State Department, lacks corroboration from other sources.

Unverified claims are prevalent, particularly from @omid_dana, who makes highly speculative assertions about an imminent US attack on Iran ("within hours" or "next Friday to Sunday"), US pressure on the UAE to seize Iran's Lavan island, and alleged direct threats by Trump to assassinate Qalibaf. These claims are not supported by other intelligence sources.

Propaganda indicators are evident across multiple actors. Press TV consistently frames events with a strong anti-US/Israeli narrative, emphasizing "US-Israeli aggression," "disastrous war on Iran," and celebrating "Iranian heroic resistance." Iranian state media channels were observed broadcasting segments where presenters handled Kalashnikov rifles, received training on weapon use, and even fired at a banner depicting the UAE flag, a clear act of state-sponsored hostile messaging and mobilization propaganda. Conversely, President Trump's social media posts ("calm before the storm" image and "fire!" animations) serve as overt propaganda intended to project dominance and signal imminent action. @omid_dana's channel, while presenting itself as an intelligence source, exhibits strong, emotionally charged anti-regime and pro-Israel biases, using derogatory language against the Iranian government and expressing explicit gratitude to the Israeli army.

Reporting gaps include a lack of detailed information regarding the "June 2025 war with Iran" (mentioned in the context of Israeli bases in Iraq) and specifics of an alleged attack on the South Korean cargo ship HMM Namu near the Strait of Hormuz. The full extent and implications of the reported halt in commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz also remain unclear.
